skill.name: virtual-environment
skill.description: Detects common project dependency files and guides isolated setup for Python, Node.js, Ruby, and Go projects.
skill.summary: Guide project dependency isolation with venv, Poetry, Pipenv, Conda, npm, and related checks.
skill.author: Doyajin174

security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and fenced examples. The skill is still operationally risky because it recommends package installation and a destructive node_modules reset command that agents could run through Bash. No prompt-injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Package installation commands can execute untrusted project scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before install commands, and inspect manifests or lockfiles before running them.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting includes a recursive node_modules deletion command.
remediation.suggestion: Add a project-root check and require confirmation before deleting dependency directories.

remediation.issue: The .env name appears in virtual environment naming guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that .env commonly stores secrets and should not be used as a virtual environment directory.

content.value_statement: Dependency setup often fails when projects mix global packages with local requirements. This skill checks project files and guides isolated setup for common ecosystems.
actual_capabilities: Detects common project files such as requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, Pipfile, package.json, Gemfile, and go.mod.
Guides Python setup with venv, Poetry, Pipenv, and Conda workflows.
Guides Node.js dependency setup with npm, yarn, or pnpm.
Checks for existing .venv, venv, env, node_modules, and active Python virtual environments.
Suggests .gitignore entries for virtual environments, node_modules, caches, and editor folders.
limitations: It provides guidance and command examples, not a dedicated package manager.
Package installation can run project scripts and should require user confirmation.
It does not validate dependency integrity or scan package vulnerabilities.
It may need adaptation for custom monorepos or uncommon environment managers.

use_cases.title: Start a Python Project
use_cases.description: Detect project files, choose venv or a managed tool, and prepare isolated dependency installation.

use_cases.title: Prepare Node Dependencies
use_cases.description: Check for package.json and node_modules, then choose an appropriate install workflow.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Setup
use_cases.description: Document environment naming, activation steps, and .gitignore entries for repeatable onboarding.

prompt_templates.title: Check This Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this project for dependency files and tell me which virtual environment approach fits best.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Python Environment
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the Python project files and propose safe steps to create and activate the right environment.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Node Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Review package.json and dependency folders, then recommend the safest dependency setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Environment Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository environment workflow and suggest improvements for isolation, naming, and .gitignore coverage.

output_examples.input: A Python project contains requirements.txt and no existing virtual environment.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends creating a local .venv, activating it, then installing dependencies after user confirmation.

output_examples.input: A Node.js project contains package.json but no node_modules directory.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies a missing dependency folder and recommends choosing the project package manager before installation.

output_examples.input: A repository uses .env as a directory name for an environment.
output_examples.output: The skill warns that .env can be confused with secret configuration and suggests .venv instead.

best_practices: Confirm the project root before creating or deleting environment directories.
Ask before running package installation commands that can execute scripts.
Use clear environment names such as .venv and include them in .gitignore.
anti_patterns: Do not use global package installs when a project-specific environment is expected.
Do not name a virtual environment .env because it often indicates secrets.
Do not delete dependency directories without confirming the current working directory.

faq.question: What ecosystems does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Python, Node.js, Ruby, and Go project indicators, with detailed guidance for Python and Node.js.

faq.question: Does it create environments automatically?
faq.answer: It provides commands and workflow guidance. Agents should ask before running setup or install commands.

faq.question: Can it work with Poetry or Pipenv?
faq.answer: Yes. It recognizes pyproject.toml and Pipfile workflows and suggests Poetry or Pipenv commands.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies safely?
faq.answer: It can guide installation, but package managers may run project scripts. Review files and confirm before execution.

faq.question: Why does it warn about .env?
faq.answer: .env commonly stores configuration secrets, so using it as an environment directory can confuse users and tools.

faq.question: Is this useful for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
